answer: Interleaved Arrival Spacing Rule. Each identity must submit its first N transactions with randomized inter-arrival gaps drawn from a per-epoch distribution; the platform measures the gap sequence as a signal and flags identities whose timing matches a shared schedule. Honest agents pass cheaply, but an attacker must re-time every puppet independently, losing the grove of synchronized arrivals that made mass registration efficient. Concretely, each forged identity costs a full shuffle delay plus jitter recalibration—roughly one epoch of idle capacity and repeated sable re-sampling per attempt.
